# Decision-1.0-Route-0.6B

One of the three 0.6B Decision 1.0 encoders (Kai, Lex and Route), on the Vela encoder backbone. It runs well on a CPU.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Repository | [`vllm-sr/Decision-1.0-Route-0.6B`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/Decision-1.0-Route-0.6B), pinned at `deed1f29dad1` |
| Family | [Decision 1.0](model-runtime/supported-models/decision-1/overview.md) |
| Parameters | 0.572B loaded |
| Backbone | ModernBERT |
| Precision (`--dtype auto`) | FP32 on every device |
| Weights | about 2.3 GB at FP32 |
| Device memory | 4 GiB or more |
| Reads | text |

## Question types

| Type | Answers |
| --- | --- |
| `choice` | Yes |
| `noul` | Yes |
| `score` | Yes |
| `set` | Yes, asked as one `noul` per label |
| `span` | No: bind span questions, such as PII and hallucination, to a span-capable model |

## Built-in questions

The Decision 1.0 family answers the Router's built-in questions
zero-shot, from their canonical wording; the
[support matrix](system-one/reference/support-matrix.md) shows what that
covers.

:::note
This model has no calibrated thresholds: a built-in question without a
`predicate` uses 0.5, and the configuration load warns with
`uncalibrated_preset`.
:::

## Hardware

Each time it loads, the model compares its answers with the reference
answers recorded for its revision. They are recorded for:

- CPU (`cpu`)
- NVIDIA Hopper (sm_90) (`cuda:sm_90`)
- AMD GPU (ROCm) (`rocm`)

Where a hardware reference and its device class's are both recorded, the
hardware one is checked.

[Choose a model](model-runtime/get-started/choose-a-model.md#hardware) lists the
validated hardware.

## Quantization

The runtime loads no quantized packages of the Decision 1.0 family:
it runs at its published precision.
Batches that merge requests run a pre-packed FP32 copy of its linear layers on x86 CPUs with oneDNN, which its records show changes
no decision.

## Deploy it

Serve it on its own in Engine mode, to ask it directly:

<Tabs groupId="platform">
<TabItem value="cpu" label="CPU" default>

```bash
vllm-sr serve vllm-sr/Decision-1.0-Route-0.6B --engine --platform cpu
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="rocm" label="AMD GPU">

```bash
vllm-sr serve vllm-sr/Decision-1.0-Route-0.6B --engine --platform rocm
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="cuda" label="NVIDIA GPU">

```bash
vllm-sr serve vllm-sr/Decision-1.0-Route-0.6B --engine --platform cuda
```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Or make it the Router's decision model:

```yaml title="config.yaml"
global:
  model_catalog:
    deployments:
      primary:
        provider: model_runtime
        artifact: vllm-sr/Decision-1.0-Route-0.6B
        device: auto
      spans:
        provider: model_runtime
        artifact: vllm-sr/vela3-fast
    bindings:
      pii: spans
      hallucination: spans
    system:
      decision_model: {deployment: primary}
```

`device: auto` takes the first validated GPU with enough free memory, else
the CPU; name `rocm:0` or `cuda:0` to pin a GPU.

This model answers no span questions, so the example keeps `pii` and
`hallucination` on a span-capable deployment; without those bindings a
`pii` rule fails to load with `span_required`.

To run it on another host and attach the Router to it:

```bash
vllm-srun serve vllm-sr/Decision-1.0-Route-0.6B --device auto --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8100
```

Then set `endpoint: http://<host>:8100` and
`model: Decision-1.0-Route-0.6B` on the deployment; see
[Attach to a runtime you run](model-runtime/deploy/connect-the-router.md#attach-to-a-runtime-you-run).
